active.name: triage nurse
active.provenance: a nurse must read each one, judge its urgency, assign a specialty, and book a slot; also 'urgency is judged by whichever nurse happens to pick the letter up'. Whether this is a dedicated team or rotating staff is an open question.

active.name: referring GP
active.provenance: GP referrals arrive as unstructured letters and faxes; the GP (and their practice) is the external sender.

active.name: shared clinical inbox
active.provenance: referrals arrive as unstructured letters and faxes into a shared clinical inbox.

active.name: senior nurse / clinical lead (accountable owner)
active.provenance: not named in the submission; inferred as the natural owner of the shared-inbox triage service. A named individual must be confirmed — this is an unverified identification, not a fact from the submission.

behavioural.name: submit referral
behavioural.provenance: GP referrals arrive as unstructured letters and faxes — the sending side of 'arrive'.

behavioural.name: receive referral
behavioural.provenance: referrals arrive into a shared clinical inbox.

behavioural.name: read referral
behavioural.provenance: a nurse must read each one.

behavioural.name: assess urgency
behavioural.provenance: judge its urgency; also 'urgency is judged by whichever nurse happens to pick the letter up' — same function, one entry.

behavioural.name: record urgency rationale
behavioural.provenance: expected change: every referral carries a recorded reason for its urgency band — currently absent ('no recorded rationale').

behavioural.name: surface red-flag symptoms
behavioural.provenance: expected change: red-flag symptoms are surfaced explicitly rather than depending on who happened to read the letter.

passive.name: referral
passive.provenance: GP referrals; takes the physical form of unstructured letters and faxes. Includes two-week-wait cancer referrals as a critical sub-type.

passive.name: urgency band
passive.provenance: its urgency band; urgency is mis-assigned today (e.g. two-week-wait cancer referrals found in the routine queue). The defined bands themselves are an open question.

passive.name: specialty
passive.provenance: assign a specialty; which specialties are in scope is an open question.

passive.name: urgency rationale
passive.provenance: a recorded reason for its urgency band; does not exist today.

passive.name: red-flag symptom
passive.provenance: red-flag symptoms to be surfaced explicitly.

passive.name: referral queue
passive.provenance: the manual queue running eleven days behind, including the routine queue where cancer referrals were found sitting.

passive.name: triage protocol
passive.provenance: open question: whether a written triage/urgency-banding protocol exists that recorded reasons must follow. Existence unconfirmed — included as a candidate object, not an established one.
